# IAEA: China's 2 MW Thorium-Based Molten Salt Reactor Achieves First Criticality

## Key Findings (recovered via secondary sources; IAEA page timed out)
- **TMSR-LF1** (2-MWth thermal experimental thorium molten salt reactor) in **Wuwei, Gansu Province**.
- Built by **Shanghai Institute of Applied Physics (SINAP)**, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS).
- **First criticality: 11 October 2023** (under operating license issued June 2023).
- **Full operation: June 2024** (100% operational capacity).
- **World's first thorium addition to a molten salt reactor: October 2024**.
- **First operational molten salt reactor globally** since US Oak Ridge program discontinued in 1969.
- Uses **thorium-uranium fuel mixture** dissolved in **fluoride salt coolant**.
- Focus: closed fuel cycles, online refueling, advanced waste management.
- Construction began **September 2018**, completed by 2022.
- **Nov 2025**: Successfully converted **thorium-232 into fissile uranium-233** (landmark achievement).
- "Currently the only operational molten-salt reactor in the world loaded with thorium fuel" (CAS).
- Scaling plan: **10-MW SMR by 2029**, **100-MWe demonstration by 2035**, full commercialization by 2040.
